page: Microsoft Azure D32d_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DDv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor running at 2.6 GHz. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance includes a bundled 1229 GB SSD.

Performance benchmarks position this server consistently in the average tier across most workloads. The Intel Xeon processor delivers a single-core Geekbench score of 1275.0 and a multi-core score of 10781.0, while Stress-ng multi-core performance reaches 29808.15. Memory bandwidth tests show 105.49 GB/sec for large block read-only operations and 46.46 GB/sec for large block write operations. However, single-threaded gzip compression is a relative weak point, registering at 23.49 GB/sec.

The CPU architecture supports AVX-512 vector instructions, including AVX512_VNNI, which aids in vector-based computations. In LLM inference tests, the server processes 1236.09 tokens/sec for a small 135M model, but drops to 4.65 tokens/sec for prompt processing on a large 70B model, highlighting a performance bottleneck for larger models due to the lack of GPU acceleration. Database operations on Passmark score 10521.57, and Redis SET operations achieve 26.79 million operations per second.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the D32d_v4 offers a balanced resource density of compute, memory, and high-capacity local SSD storage. This makes it suitable for workloads requiring fast local scratch space alongside moderate compute, such as relational databases, web serving, software compilation, and general-purpose enterprise applications.
